The brief before the build

Every project that went wrong for us went wrong in the first conversation. What we now ask before scoping anything, and why the order matters.

A brief is not a list of features. It is a description of the situation the work has to change.

Three questions, in order

  1. What happens today? The current process, in the words of the person who runs it.
  2. What would be different if this worked? Not a metric, a scene. Who is doing what, that they cannot do now.
  3. What must not change? The constraints that are actually load-bearing: a regulator, a partner system, a habit the team will not give up.

Only after those three do we talk about scope, and only after scope do we talk about tools.

Why the order matters

Starting with tools produces a project that fits the tool. Starting with the situation produces a project that fits the organization. The second kind gets used.
